messages:
ara: Quick heads-up — ran an A/B perf sweep this morning for the new interleaved batch scheduler + geo-throttle queue policy. Results look mixed.
ara: Setup: 3 clusters (us-east, eu-west, ap-south), interleaved batch formation enabled, per-az token credits, cross-az borrowing allowed but limited. KV cache warm on us-east only.
ara: Observations: us-east p50/p95 improved ~6-8%, ap-south similar. eu-west p95 increased ~18% under burst load when cross-az borrowing kicked in. CPU spikes on the routing proxy aligned with many small batches being formed.
jamie: Can you paste the trace/profiler snippet? sounds like batching shape changed and kernel selection maybe toggling more often.
ara: Paste of flame snippet (trimmed):
```
route_handler.handle_request  40%
batch_assembler.coalesce    22%
kernel_selector.switch_path 15%
kv_cache.lookup_miss         9%
gpu_enqueue/kv_upload        6%
```
ara: Notice kernel_selector.delta calls spike when batch size oscillates between 8 and 64 tokens — looks like heuristic flip-flop.
taylor: Hmm. so interleaving reduces latency for colocated load but causes unstable batch size distribution across zones when tokens are low. Did you try increasing token_budget_target for eu-west?
ara: Yep — bumped per-az token_budget_target from 1200 -> 1800 for eu-west in one variant. That reduced kernel thrash but increased tail a bit because more cross-az borrow occurred. tradeoff between local batching and cross-az traffic.
mike: Can we add a short-circuit: prefer local kernel path if estimated extra latency from cross-az > 6ms? That would avoid borrowing when marginal benefit is small.
sophia: Also saw KV cache churn: eu-west had higher KV miss rate because most of the prefix cache is populated in us-east training traffic. During spill, we push more cold state to GPUs in eu-west which increases first-token latency.
ara: Agreed. Two mitigations I tested:
- geo-prefetch small hot prefixes into remote KV during low load window
- split token buckets: reserve small local bucket that cannot be borrowed
ara: Config snippet I used:
```
queue_policy:
  interleaved: true
  max_tokens_per_batch: 2048
  local_reserve_ratio: 0.12
  cross_az_burst_reclaim: 0.10
kernel_selector:
  soft_switch_threshold_ms: 5
  prefer_local_on_cost: true
token_buckets:
  global_target: "1500"
  per_az_target: {"us-east":"1600","eu-west":"1800","ap-south":"1400"}
```
jamie: prefer_local_on_cost + soft_switch_threshold looks good. Can we measure how often prefer_local_on_cost prevents a kernel switch? add a stat counter.
taylor: Also add queue watermark metrics: queue_local_fill, crossborrow_events, kv_miss_rate_per_az — we need to correlate before/after.
sophia: For KV prefetch, be careful about memory pressure on remote GPUs. Keep prefetch window tiny (top-20 prefixes) and LRU them aggressively.
mike: Long-term: maybe adjust kernel selection to be stable across a small band — hysteresis instead of immediate flip when batch size crosses a threshold.
ara: +1. I prototyped hysteresis: require two consecutive sampling intervals beyond threshold before switching. Reduced kernel thrash by ~65% in the run.
ara: Next steps I'm proposing:
- instrument metrics counters jamie/taylor suggested (1 day)
- enable prefer_local_on_cost + hysteresis in canary (us-east + eu-west small % traffic) (2 days)
- run KV prefetch experiment on eu-west during low-traffic window (1 day)
- measure end-to-end p50/p95 and cross-az bandwidth (1 day)
ara: Anyone object to me putting this into a short canary tomorrow? I think it's low-risk if traffic % is small.
jamie: +1 from me. add a kill-switch flag.
taylor: +1. If eu-west tail creeps again, rollback immediately.
sophia: +1. I'll scope the prefetch to memory budget and send a patch.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: interleaved-scheduler-canary -> eng-runtime-canary @ 2026-03-18T03:30Z (flag: geo.prefers_local)
ara: Thanks team — I'll open a PR with the metric names and the canary playbook.
